title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime is zero fibre dimension at that point
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset T$ be prime and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Put $F=T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\overline{\mathfrak q}\in\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be the unique prime contracting to $\mathfrak q$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Then $\varphi$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] if and only if $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}\operatorname{Spec}F=0$, where dimension at a point is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

source.place: Tag 0397, label lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0, applied to Spec T -> Spec R; the second proof identifies isolated points with points of dimension zero in the locally Noetherian fibre.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$. Choose finite $R$-algebra generators $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ of $T$. The elements $t_i\otimes1$ generate $F$ as a $k$-algebra: every element of the tensor product is a finite sum of pure tensors, and if $t=P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ then $t\otimes a=aP_k(t_1\otimes1,\ldots,t_n\otimes1)$, where the coefficients of $P_k$ are the images in $k$ of the coefficients of $P$. Thus $F$ is a finite type algebra over the field $k$; no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ or $T$ is needed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] with $A=F$ and the field $k$. It gives that $F$ is Noetherian and that every descending chain of closed subsets of $X$ stabilizes.

proof.text: The one-member affine cover $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$ makes $X$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. It is also quasi-compact: if an open cover had no finite subcover, successively choose a member not contained in the union of the previously chosen finitely many members. The complements of these successive finite unions would form a strictly descending infinite chain of closed subsets, contradicting step 2. Consequently $X$ is a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact).

proof.text: Assume $\varphi$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. By [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], the singleton $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is an open neighbourhood in $X$. Its only nonempty irreducible closed subset is itself, so its Krull dimension is zero. Every neighbourhood of $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is nonempty and has nonnegative dimension. The minimum defining dimension at the point is therefore exactly zero.

source.place: Tag 0H7C, lemma-isolated-dim-0-locally-noetherian, first implication; Topology Tag 0055, definition-Krull

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}X=0$. Since dimension at a point is the minimum of the dimensions of its open neighbourhoods, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ with $\dim U=0$. Regard $U$ as an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $X$ from step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $U$ is Noetherian, so [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] applies and its topology is discrete. In particular $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $U$. Since $U$ is open in $X$, a subset open in $U$ is open in $X$, by the definition of the subspace topology.

The openness of $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ obtained in step 5 is precisely quasi-finiteness of $\varphi$ at $\mathfrak q$ by [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Together with step 4 this proves the asserted equivalence.
